newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom lower on decree, Russian shares seen flat.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom lower on decree, Russian shares seen flat.

text.p: Russian natural gas producer Gazprom sagged in early trade on Thursday on news foreigners would no longer be able to buy cheap local shares, traders said, predicting a lacklustre day for other leading Russian shares.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index opened slightly down at 351.27 after closing on Wednesday at 351.40.

"It's rather lethargic -- it looks like we're in for that for the rest of the week," said ING Barings chief equities trader Peter Kizenko, saying the RTS index of 22 leading shares would be mostly unchanged. "There hasn't been a liquidity move into Russia at this point."
Market leader UES slipped to $0.3100 at 0940 GMT from $0.3104 on Wednesday while regional utility Mosenergo firmed slightly to $1.2700 from $1.2685.
Dealers said a presidential decree on Gazprom, signed late on Wednesday, limited to nine percent the share of the world's biggest natural gas producer that may be held by foreigners.
"Any change like that, when there's new legislation, the market reacts negatively," said Renaissance Capital trader Vladimir Chkikvadze.

Gazprom requires overseas investors to keep their Gazprom holdings as more expensive American Depositary Shares, but many investors have used Russian-registered subsidiaries to buy Gazprom shares legally on the local market.
The decree will not force current holders of the bargain stock to sell their shares, as had been rumoured.
Gazprom fell to $0.5900 from $0.6495 and Kizenko said it could sag lower, although it might find support around $0.60.
He expected the Gazprom ADS price to rise, in contrast, on recent restructuring moves and rosy 1996 financial results.
But traders predicted a slow rest of the day and week for the market with investor interest concentrated firmly on less liquid second and third tier stock.
